body: The first paragraph talks about the need for "access to test systems (including access to at least one account in each role),", however I think it might be fair to say that 2 accounts would be needed for testing horizontal privilege escalation between users of the same role - several ASVS requirements indicates that such tests should be done, e.g., testing that a user only can create/update data for their own profile and not for other users (unless explicitly authorized to do so)

comments.body:
That depends highly on the application design.
Take for example a marketplace like ebay: You log in as user A for which you have the credentials and then somehow manage to create an offer in the name of account B. Do you really need access to account B in order to verify that there's something afoul?

If full access to the escalated account was neccessary, the attacker would need to gain that same level of access through the problem.

title: Guidance for Certifying Organizations - may need 2 accounts for testing horizontal priv esc?
